## Source research and next candidate

Reader question: why do live host/helper processes and running conversations have different counts in AgentSight, and how is a shared host associated with a conversation? Product PR #273 fixes prior stale host association and running-count inflation. This is **master-only, not a released v1.0.35 claim**.

- [PR #273](https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/agentsight/pull/273) and the exact commit describe ranking session candidates by recency then confidence instead of accepting the first path when a long-lived host holds multiple conversation logs open.
- [sessionState.mjs](https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/agentsight/blob/2b16f697f557a8694e423ccf96d9cd5908222c91/ext/web/lib/sessionState.mjs): a live process row has a positive numeric PID; a session row additionally has a nonempty session ID. Running requires a parsed last-message timestamp less than 180,000 ms old, or a missing/unparseable time (compatibility fallback). A future timestamp also passes the age predicate; do not call the status proof of current computation. Exactly 180,000 ms is outside the strict threshold.
- [fleetData.test.mjs](https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/agentsight/blob/2b16f697f557a8694e423ccf96d9cd5908222c91/ext/web/lib/fleetData.test.mjs) synthetic fixture: one current session plus two helper rows counts as one running session, four processes, 8 summed CPU percentage points and 150 MB summed RSS. These are test assertions, not measurements. The helpers remain in resource totals.
- Existing progressive-fleet article owns latency and partial rendering; native discovery owns directory enumeration; top-counter article owns native/capture summary provenance. A running-state/host association analysis has distinct decision semantics, but compare the correlation-confidence article in full before selecting new canonical URL. Do not publish a duplicate; enrich that canonical if it already owns the question.
- Proposed acceptance if content is selected: one source-pinned rendered article or major canonical refresh, corresponding Blog metadata and sitemap, exact CI and deployment, independent public check. Preserve homepage GA4, release claims, other routes and protected files. Roll back only the resulting focused content squash if needed.
